prompt:
You are a data analyst. Use only the data below; show arithmetic; respond directly.

Records: 123, 4567, 89, 2341, 4005, 765, 9876, 223, 6789, 878

Report: total, count, average, min, max, median.

You are a GTM analyst. Use only the data below. Never invent facts, deals, companies, or numbers. Show your arithmetic. Cite company aliases exactly as given.

Pipeline summary: COMMIT = 42 deals totaling $127,149. BEST_CASE = 27 deals totaling $89,312. The two largest commit deals are C-42F1A9 and C-27B307. All other stages excluded.

Build the Q3 weighted forecast: 100% of COMMIT + 35% of BEST_CASE. Give totals and the counts; mention the two large commit aliases.

You are a GTM/revenue-operations analyst. Use only the data provided. Never invent facts, deals, companies, or numbers. If data is missing, say so explicitly. Show your arithmetic. Cite deal aliases exactly as given.

Open deals in the default pipeline, close date in Q3 (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30):

COMMIT:
- Deal-AAA111  Acme Corp     $12,000  close 2026-08-15
- Deal-BBB222  Globex        $8,500   close 2026-09-01
- Deal-CCC333  Initech       $6,200   close 2026-07-20

BEST_CASE:
- Deal-DDD444  Umbrella      $20,000  close 2026-09-10
- Deal-EEE555  Hooli         $10,000  close 2026-08-28

Excluded (outside quarter or disqualified): Deal-FFF666 $5,000 close 2026-11-01; Deal-GGG777 $4,000 close 2026-06-15.

Build the Q3 weighted forecast: 100% of COMMIT plus 35% of BEST_CASE. Report: commit total, best-case total, weighted forecast total, count of commit deals, count of best-case deals, count and dollar amount excluded. Flag any deal missing a close date or owner if present (none are).

You are a GTM/revenue-operations analyst. Use only the data provided. Never invent facts. Show your arithmetic.

Stage history snapshot (12 deals). Stages in order: DS1 < DS2 < DS3 < DS4 < DS5. A 'regression' = a later stage-entry timestamp earlier than a prior stage's entry.

- Deal-A1: DS1 2026-07-01, DS2 2026-07-05, DS3 2026-07-09  (clean)
- Deal-A2: DS1 2026-07-02, DS2 2026-07-06, DS3 missing     (missing stage)
- Deal-A3: DS1 2026-07-03, DS2 2026-07-04, DS3 2026-07-04  (same-day, not a regression)
- Deal-A4: DS1 2026-07-05, DS2 2026-07-03                  (regression: DS2 before DS1)
- Deal-A5: DS1 2026-07-06, DS2 2026-07-08                  (clean)
- Deal-A6: DS1 2026-07-07, DS2 missing                     (missing stage)
- Deal-A7: DS1 2026-07-08, DS2 2026-07-09, DS3 2026-07-10, DS4 2026-07-11  (clean)
- Deal-A8: DS1 2026-07-09, DS2 2026-07-09                  (same-day, clean)
- Deal-A9: DS1 2026-07-10, DS2 2026-07-08                  (regression)
- Deal-B1: DS1 2026-07-11, DS2 2026-07-12                  (clean)
- Deal-B2: DS1 2026-07-12, DS2 2026-07-13, DS3 2026-07-14  (clean)
- Deal-B3: DS1 2026-07-13, DS2 2026-07-14                  (clean)

Report: total deals, count with a missing stage timestamp, count of regressions, names of the regression deals, and whether every deal has a DS1 timestamp.

You are a GTM analyst. Use only the data below. Show arithmetic.

AE activity and outcomes, Q3 to date:

- Alex:   120 calls, 45 demos, 12 closed-won, $310,000 won
- Jordan: 200 calls, 30 demos,  8 closed-won, $180,000 won
- Sam:     90 calls, 38 demos, 10 closed-won, $265,000 won

Compute for each rep: demo rate (demos/calls, as %), win rate on demos (closed-won/demos, as %), average deal size (won/closed-won). Rank the three reps by average deal size, highest first. Round percentages to 1 decimal.

You are a GTM analyst. Use only the data below. Never invent facts.

Closed-lost deals this quarter with rep-entered loss reason and a transcript excerpt:

- Deal-K1 ($30k): reason='Price'. Transcript: 'Your renewal quote is double what we budgeted; procurement said no.'
- Deal-K2 ($55k): reason='Price'. Transcript: 'We went with Vendor X — their feature set matched ours but yours was fine on price.'
- Deal-K3 ($18k): reason='Timing'. Transcript: 'Budget froze this quarter, revisit in Q1.'
- Deal-K4 ($40k): reason='Price'. Transcript: 'The per-seat price is 40% over our cap.'

Task: for each deal, state whether the transcript supports or contradicts the rep-entered reason, with a one-line justification. Then give total closed-lost dollars where the entered reason appears contradicted.

You are a chief of staff. Compress the update below into exactly 3 bullet points for the CEO's weekly Slack digest. Each bullet max 20 words. Preserve every number. No new facts.

Update: Pipeline grew from $2.1M to $2.6M week-over-week, driven by 14 new opportunities created by the outbound team. Win rate dipped from 32% to 28% as two enterprise deals pushed to next quarter, representing $400k in deferred ARR. The CS team onboarded 9 new customers, the fastest week this year, and support ticket volume fell 15% after the new help-center launch.

You are an SRE writing a postmortem. Use only the events below. Produce a chronological timeline (HH:MM format), then state total time-to-detect and time-to-resolve in minutes.

Events:
- 09:41 Deploy of service v2.3.1 completed
- 09:47 First elevated error-rate alert fires (6 minutes after deploy)
- 09:52 On-call acknowledges page
- 10:05 Rollback to v2.3.0 initiated
- 10:11 Error rate returns to baseline; incident closed

Respond with the timeline, TTD, and TTR only.

You are a CS ops analyst. Use only the policy and accounts below. Show your reasoning briefly.

Save-offer policy: eligible if (a) ARR >= $20,000 AND (b) health score >= 40 AND (c) no open severity-1 ticket.

Accounts requesting cancellation:
- Acme:     ARR $52,000, health 71, no open sev-1
- Globex:   ARR $18,500, health 66, no open sev-1
- Initech:  ARR $88,000, health 35, no open sev-1
- Umbrella: ARR $41,000, health 58, one open sev-1
- Hooli:    ARR $25,000, health 49, no open sev-1

List each account as ELIGIBLE or INELIGIBLE and which criterion failed (if any). Then state how many are eligible.

You are a marketing ops analyst. Use only the data below. Show arithmetic.

Q3 sourced pipeline by channel:
- Paid search:  $420,000 across 35 opps
- Organic:      $310,000 across 41 opps
- Events:       $180,000 across 12 opps
- Partners:     $90,000 across 7 opps

Total marketing spend this quarter: $250,000.

Compute: total sourced pipeline, pipeline per channel as % of total (1 decimal), average opp size per channel, and overall pipeline-to-spend ratio (e.g. 4.0x).
